topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the series on cancer causation and outlines the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Environmental Drivers of Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises from the interplay between intrinsic biological processes, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures reflected in global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various infectious agents drive oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of pathogen interplay.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental and dietary agents undergo metabolic activation or energy transfer to cause direct DNA damage and mutation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Non-Mutagenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the multi-stage model of carcinogenesis by distinguishing non-mutagenic tumor promoters and inflammatory microenvironments from initiating mutagens.

topics.label: Host Developmental State and Carcinogen Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cellular proliferation states and specific life stages modulate tissue susceptibility to carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess their cancer risk.
